text:
alex: Weekly check-in — quick error-rate breakdown for acct cohort A (onboarding batch). Notable: 5xx spike yesterday 02:14-02:38 UTC. Top failing endpoints called out below.

maya: Thanks — can you paste the top-line numbers?

alex: Sure. High-level (24h window): 5xx: 3.8% (baseline 0.4%), timeouts: 1.6%, rate-limits: 0.9%. Biggest hit between 02:14-02:38 UTC.

maya: Oof. Which endpoints?

alex: Top failing URIs by count: 
- /v1/generate (orig): 42% of 5xx 
- /v1/chat/stream (ws fallback): 22% 
- /v1/embeddings/batch: 14% 
- /v1/re-rank: 9% 
- /v1/prompt-validate: 6%

jon: any deploys or config changes around 02:10?

alex: There was a dedicated runtime patch rolled at 02:05 (eng-runtime). Canary to prod completed 02:12.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: runtime-patch-2026-02-05 @02:12 UTC — canary->prod (sha: f3a1b2c).

jon: looks suspiciously correlated. I pulled a few logs for /v1/generate:
```
[02:16:11] 504 gateway timeout for req id=acct-8902-req-1293 route=/v1/generate
[02:16:12] 503 service unavailable - kvcache miss spike
[02:17:05] 500 internal error: cuda OOM on shard 2 for seq_len 1024
```

maya: Account 8902 was onboarding heavy tokens that window (long seqs).

alex: Also saw repeated 429s for /v1/chat/stream, but most were from a single integration sending many parallel streams.

sara: Any mitigations we can push short-term to reduce renewal risk?

jon: Short-term action suggestions: 
- rollback runtime patch to previous build (if safe) OR pin the shard kernel to older kernel for that pool
- add retries with jitter for 504s and 5xx (client-side), temp throttle for parallel streams from offending integration
- for OOM: enforce max_seq_len=512 via gateway for onboarding cohort A until we confirm memory profile

maya: I'll message the onboarding partner to throttle their parallel ingestion and limit seq length.

alex: I'll flag this to account team — CCing renewal owner. Suggested comms: "we noted an elevated error rate during your import job; we've taken temporary throttles and are rolling config to stabilize. We'll follow up with full RCA."

sara: Can you also capture sample request IDs for CS to attach to the ticket?

alex: Sample IDs: acct-8902-req-1293, acct-8902-req-1301, acct-8902-req-1420, acct-8910-req-2102. Adding stack traces to the incident ticket.

jon: I created a short runbook: 
1) rollback runtime-patch-2026-02-05 if errors persist after config change
2) scale pool 3 -> 4 GPUs for 1 hour to drain backlog
3) force prefix/KV cache warm on hotspots (commands below)
```
# warm cache
curl -X POST https://internal-api/ops/warm_cache -d '{"paths":["/v1/generate","/v1/chat/stream"]}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS'
```

maya: ETA on warming + throttles?

jon: Warm + throttle pushes in next 10m. Scaling in 15 if we still see >1.5% 5xx.

alex: Account owner and renewal lead updated. Next check-in in 2 hours or earlier if rollback.

sara: Also, capture cost impact for the window — token burn spike might affect billing conversation.

alex: noted. Preliminary numbers: ~3.2x normal token consumption during the import window for cohort A. I'll include in the follow-up.

maya: Thanks team. I'll draft the customer note and include the sample IDs + mitigation steps.

alex: Action items: 
- maya: customer comms + partner throttle (owner)
- jon: throttle + cache warm + monitor (ops owner)
- alex: attach logs, sample IDs, update renewal owner

deploy-bot: monitor alert: 5xx rate now 0.8% (down from 3.8%) — continuing to watch. :white_check_mark:

maya: Good progress. We'll regroup if it creeps back up. :thumbsup:
